summary: Grenada is visa-free for the great majority of visitors: CARICOM nationals move freely for up to six months, and citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada and most Commonwealth countries are admitted for up to 90 days on arrival. Everyone else needs a visitor's visa arranged through a Grenadian mission before traveling. There is no visa on arrival and no eVisa.

passportValidity.text: Carry a passport valid for at least six months on the day you arrive. Immigration will often accept a passport valid for the length of the visit, but airlines apply the six-month rule as a matter of course and can refuse boarding.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (yellow card)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you are arriving from, or have recently transited, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — mainly parts of tropical Africa and South America. Travelers coming directly from Europe, North America or elsewhere in the Caribbean do not need one to enter Grenada.

source.name: Government of Grenada — entry and immigration information

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked at the border, but it matters here: Grenada's public hospital handles routine care only, and serious cases are flown to Barbados, Trinidad or Miami at the patient's expense. Make sure any policy covers medical evacuation and hurricane disruption.

source.name: Government of Grenada — entry and immigration information

onwardTicket.text: Immigration officers routinely ask visitors for a confirmed return or onward ticket and the address where they will be staying. Have both to hand on the arrival card.

source.name: Government of Grenada — entry and immigration information

proofOfFunds.text: No published minimum. Officers may ask how you intend to support yourself, particularly for long stays or open-ended itineraries.

source.name: Government of Grenada — entry and immigration information

declarations.name: Immigration and Customs Declaration
declarations.submitWindow: On arrival, or shortly before travel where the electronic form is offered
declarations.text: Every arriving passenger completes an immigration and customs declaration covering their address in Grenada, length of stay and dutiable goods. Grenada has been shifting this onto an online form. Check with your airline before you fly, and be ready to complete the paper card handed out on board.

source.name: Government of Grenada — entry and immigration information

currencyLimits.text: Cash and negotiable instruments worth about USD 10,000 or more (or the EC dollar equivalent) must be declared to Customs on arrival and departure. Confirm the current threshold with Grenada Customs before traveling with large sums.

source.name: Government of Grenada — entry and immigration information

notes: Firearms and ammunition may not be brought in without a permit issued in advance — even a single stray round found in luggage is treated as a criminal matter.
Camouflage-patterned clothing is restricted across much of the eastern Caribbean and can be confiscated on arrival; leave it at home.
Fresh produce, plants, seeds and meat are controlled to protect Grenada's spice and agricultural industry. Declare anything of the sort.
Penalties for drug offenses are severe and apply to visitors exactly as they do to residents.

payments.text: Hotels, restaurants and the larger supermarkets in St George's and Grand Anse take cards. Local buses, market vendors, beach vendors and small rum shops are cash-only. US dollars are accepted almost everywhere, but change usually comes back in EC dollars.

safety.text: Grenada is one of the calmer islands in the Caribbean and violent crime rarely involves visitors. The realistic risks are opportunistic theft from beaches and rental cars, strong currents on the Atlantic (east) coast, and hurricane season disruption.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Grenada Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: January to April is the dry season, with reliable sun and calm Caribbean-coast seas. August brings Spicemas carnival in the middle of the wetter months, and hurricane season runs June to November.

tips.text: Hurricane season runs June to November, peaking in August and September. Grenada sits at the southern edge of the usual storm track but is not immune — Hurricane Beryl devastated Carriacou and Petite Martinique in 2024. Insurance covering storm disruption is worth having.

Driving is on the left and visitors need a Grenadian temporary driving permit, bought through the police or your rental company on presentation of your home license. Renting without one invalidates your cover.

The East Caribbean dollar is pegged to the US dollar at about EC$2.70 to US$1. US notes are accepted widely, but you will normally get change in EC dollars at that rate, so paying in US cash for small items is rarely a bargain.

An airport departure tax and security fee applies when leaving Grenada. It is normally bundled into the ticket price, but confirm with your airline rather than assuming you will not be asked at check-in.

Grenada runs a citizenship-by-investment program. If you hold a Grenadian passport obtained that way, expect closer scrutiny when applying for visas elsewhere. The EU in particular has tightened its treatment of Caribbean CBI passports, and visa-free arrangements have been reviewed.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Grenada?
faq.answer: Most likely not. Grenada admits citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and most Commonwealth countries visa-free for up to 90 days, and CARICOM nationals for six months. If your nationality is not covered, you must obtain a visitor's visa from a Grenadian mission or honorary consulate before you fly — Grenada has no visa on arrival and no eVisa.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Grenada without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-free visitors are normally admitted for up to 90 days, though the officer writes the actual period on your entry stamp and it can be shorter if your ticket says so. Extensions are handled by the Immigration Department in St George's and should be applied for before your stamp expires.

faq.question: Is there an arrival form for Grenada?
faq.answer: Yes. Every passenger completes an immigration and customs declaration with their address in Grenada and length of stay. Grenada has been moving this to an online form, so check with your airline before departure — otherwise the paper card is handed out on the aircraft.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Grenada?
faq.answer: Only if you are arriving from or transiting a yellow fever risk country in tropical Africa or South America. Travelers coming from Europe, North America or elsewhere in the Caribbean are not asked for one.

faq.question: Can I drive in Grenada on my own license?
faq.answer: Not on its own. You need a Grenadian temporary driving permit, issued on the spot by the police or your rental company against a valid home license. Driving is on the left, roads are narrow and steep, and goats are a genuine hazard.

faq.question: Does CARICOM free movement apply in Grenada?
faq.answer: Yes. Grenada is a member of CARICOM and the OECS, so nationals of member states are granted a definite entry of up to six months on arrival, without a visa and generally without needing to show onward tickets in the way other visitors do.
